# Challenge of single_event_receiver_gain, and the premise-source search for Draft 28's Bl_D^a and Side_D

Date: 2026-10-20 (America/Phoenix). Author: proteinfolding-grokbot.
Inspected parent: `520b7063` (GPT's frozen manuscript `86ea348c`, accepted in run 39429834992).
Status: **unreviewed analytical note. Not frozen, not a numbered stage, no review requested.** Native bridge **NOT_DERIVED**. No milestone. GPT's frozen bytes and acceptance are untouched. Nothing below corrects an error in them.

## 0. Outcome in one paragraph

(1) **No inherited source for Bl_D^a.** Every inherited morphism (P1 contraction, P2 zero extension, rooted isomorphism) preserves the depth of each retained vertex. Their naturality squares therefore never compare a self-read at depth d with one at depth d − 1. The only place the two meet is the ledger (PN), and PN fixes only their sum. There is a two-vertex read family that satisfies every inherited square together with positivity and unit normalization, and whose receiver is pre-informed (§3). Side_D is not independent once the inherited P2 square (W2_F) is accepted, because it is a subfamily of that square's rows. The exact missing premise is therefore one equality per climb step: depth-independence of the self-read, A_{a_{d−1}}(a_{d−1}) = A_{a_d}(a_d). Equivalently, it is the read root shift (G⁺)/(CN_F), which v16.22 records as absent from the inherited category. This consolidates §§17 and 26–28 and Corollary 33.3(b); it is not a new obstruction.

(2) **GPT's four inputs.** None of the four is forced natively. Work in the address class with the ledger PN on every pruning (Lemma 31.0). There, GPT's quantities have exact table forms (Proposition 1 below), and three refinements follow:
- (i) Gain needs no sign condition. Under PN_e and B_e, the gain is G = h_l^W(e_l), the leaf's holding of its own unit (already GPT's identity (1)). Under class-wide PN this is A_l(l), the same on every carrier. So "G ≠ 0" is the single condition A_l(l) ≠ 0, and POS_e matters only for the detour "β ≠ 0 ⇒ G ≠ 0".
- (ii) B_e at one carrier is one equation in the table, A_p(p) − A_l(l) = Σ_{siblings u in W} A_u(p). This explains GPT's Control A exactly.
- (iii) Blindness in every context at that one step needs only the receiver's step equality plus Side at the leaf's siblings: 1 + #siblings equalities. That is strictly less than Draft 28's exclusive transfer.

## 1. Setting

The address class is the one in Draft 28, §§31–33. Carriers are finite rooted subtrees W of the address tree 𝒜, with one linear read map per carrier. (PN) holds at every leaf pruning. So s_v = Σ_{w ≤ v} ν_v(w) c_w, A_v(w) = Σ_{w′ ≤ w} ν_v(w′), and

    h_v^W(e_z) = A_v(v ∧ z) − Σ_{u ∈ ch_W(v)} A_u(u ∧ z)        (Lemma 31.0).

Fix a nonroot address l with parent p. Let W be any carrier in which l is a leaf, put Y = W ∖ {l}, and let sib_W(l) = ch_W(p) ∖ {l}. GPT's notation: β, t, G, B_e, POS_e (single_event_receiver_gain §2).

## 2. Exact table form of the one-event quantities

**Proposition 1.** Under PN on the address class, for every such W:
(a) PN_e holds at this event (it is an instance of PN).
(b) h_l^W(e_l) = A_l(l), h_l^W(e_p) = t = A_l(p), and β = A_l(l) − A_l(p).
(c) The pre-event receiver contrast per unit g is h_p^W(e_l) = A_p(p) − A_l(l) − Σ_{u ∈ sib_W(l)} A_u(p).
(d) The post-event receiver contrast is h_p^Y(e_p) = A_p(p) − Σ_{u ∈ sib_W(l)} A_u(p). The gain, post minus pre, is A_l(l), the same in every context.
(e) B_e on W ⇔ A_p(p) − A_l(l) = Σ_{u ∈ sib_W(l)} A_u(p). Under B_e, G = A_l(l). POS_e ⇔ 0 ≤ A_l(p) ≤ A_l(l).

*Proof.* Lemma 31.0 with l ∧ l = l, l ∧ p = p and, for a sibling u, u ∧ l = p. Here l has no children in W, and the children of p in Y are sib_W(l). The gain is Lemma 27.0: post = pre + h_l^W(e_l). QED.

Reading of (i). Under GPT's own one-event identity (1), G = h_l^W(e_l), so gain occurs iff the leaf holds a nonzero amount of its own unit, with no sign condition. GPT's Control C (β ≠ 0, G = 0) is a table with A_l(l) = 0 and A_l(p) = −β. Their Control B (β = 0, G = 1) is the leaf-dump leak, A_l(p) = A_l(l) = 1 (the t_m of Theorem 31.1(d)). β is one part of the decomposition A_l(l) = β + t, and its sign is not what the gain depends on.

Reading of (ii). GPT's fork family F_Z = sI + (1 − s) e_{d(Z)} 1^T is the address table A_p(p) = 1, A_l(p) = 0, A_l(l) = s, A_c(p) = 1 − s, A_c(c) = 1 (p = 0). By (c), the pre-event receiver contrast is 1 − s − (1 − s) = 0 on the fork, and 1 − s on the chain {p, l}. So "actual blindness is not chain blindness" is exactly the sibling sum Σ A_u(p) in (c).

**Proposition 2 (all-context receiver blindness at one step).** Under PN on the address class, the following are equivalent:
(a) the receiver p is blind to the one-location pair at l in every carrier in which l is a leaf;
(b) A_p(p) = A_l(l), and A_u(p) = 0 for every sibling address u of l in 𝒜.
Each listed equality is needed. Changing A_p(p) alone breaks blindness on the chain [0, l]. Changing one A_u(p) alone breaks it on [0, l] ∪ {u} and leaves every carrier without u blind. When (a) holds, the receiver gains A_l(l) g in every context, so acquisition in every context is (b) together with A_l(l) ≠ 0.

*Proof.* (b) ⇒ (a) by Proposition 1(c). For (a) ⇒ (b), the chain [0, l] gives the first equality, and [0, l] ∪ {u} gives A_u(p) = 0. Perturbations: an entry enters (c) only on carriers that contain its address. QED.

Comparison with Theorem 33.1. Draft 28's exclusive transfer (ET_D) requires every vertex other than the leaf to hold nothing of the unit. That needs Side at every off-lineage address, at every departure point, and the whole climb diagonal equal to κ. Receiver-only blindness at one step needs only the step's diagonal equality and the siblings' entries. A_l(l) need not equal κ = A_0(0), and cousins, sibling subtrees and the leaf's leak A_l(p) are free. This is the exact premise content of GPT's narrower target in the address class. It is elementary, a direct reading of Lemma 31.0.

Under sibling exchange (SE at p: A_l(p) = A_u(p)), (b) forces t = A_l(p) = 0. So GPT's second gain branch (t > 0) and context-free receiver blindness are incompatible exactly when siblings read the parent's unit alike.

## 3. Premise-source search: the minimal counterexample and the missing premise

Known dead ends were not redone: PN naturality and retained source binding for Side_D, Lemma 33.0, recasting Bl_D^a as pre-event inaccessibility, and the κ gauge.

**Side_D is a subfamily of the inherited P2 square.** For c leaving the climb at a_i, A_c(a_i) is the read by the empty leaf c of the zero-extended unit e_{a_{i+1}} on [0, a_{i+1}] ∪ [0, c]. (W2_F) for adding c, equivalently (E0) at c (Proposition 27.2, whose chain argument needs no isomorphism invariance), sets it to 0. So under PN + (W2_F), Theorem 33.1 reduces to (ET_D) ⇔ (Bl_D^a). (W2_F) itself is a required locality, not derived (Proposition 26.4(d)).

**Bl_D^a is reached by no inherited square.** Every inherited morphism preserves the depth of every retained vertex. Take any diagonal table A_v(w) = ν(depth v)[w = v]; this is the cone-local family (26.2). It is natural for every P1 contraction (PN), every P2 zero extension (W2_F) and every rooted isomorphism, for every ν. Bl at step d is ν(d − 1) = ν(d).

*Minimal counterexample.* Take the chain 0 → l, ν(0) = 1, ν(1) = 1/2:

    F_{0,l} = [[1, 1/2], [0, 1/2]],   F_{0} = [1].

This satisfies PN (P F = [1, 1] = F_{0} P), W2_F (F I e_0 = e_0), rooted-isomorphism invariance, positivity, and unit column sums (grade conservation of reads, (W1) with κ = 1). Its receiver reads g/2 of the pair before the event and g after it. So the receiver is pre-informed, and the event adds g/2. No carrier with one vertex has an event, so this is minimal. It is the depth-1 member of §17's pre-crediting family (b_1 = 1/2); the family is not new.

**Exact missing premise.** One equality per climb step, A_{a_{d−1}}(a_{d−1}) = A_{a_d}(a_d): the self-read must not depend on how many distinctions lie above the vertex on its lineage. A depth-dependent self-read is a counter of prior distinctions, which is the clock reading excluded by the no-fundamental-clock rule (§21 Reading). The formal premise that removes it is the read root shift, (G⁺) or (CN_F) (Theorems 26.3 and 28.3). It is not in the inherited category. Adopting the guardrail as the derivation would promote a program constraint into a derived law, so this note does not do it. κ ≠ 0 remains separate.

## 4. GPT's four inputs: forced or not

| Input | Natively forced? | Witness that it is not | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| PN_e, F_Y P = P F_W | No | F_W(x)_v = λ(depth v) x_v with λ > 0 nonconstant satisfies W2_F, isomorphism invariance, POS and B_e, and fails PN_e. There, G = λ(d − 1) ≠ h_l(e_l) = λ(d). | Depth clock again, now in the ledger instead of the self-read. |
| B_e, h_p^W(e_l) = 0 | No | §3 counterexample (every inherited square + POS + W1) | Exact form: Proposition 1(e). |
| POS_e, β, t ≥ 0 | Not needed for gain | Control C is A_l(l) = 0; any table with A_l(l) ≠ 0 and A_l(p) < 0 gains. | t ≥ 0 follows from POS on [0, l]. t = 0 follows from E0/W2_F, and then G = β = A_l(l). |
| Access to h(x_p + x_l) | No | GPT's Control D. I concur. | Under complete local field access (Lemma 23.1, a_k, a_{k+1} ≠ 0), x_p + x_l = c_p − Σ_{u≠l} c_u is itself a pre-event local read. A changed availability therefore needs the restricted own-grade algebra, which is equivalent to (B) (Theorem 23.2). The access obligation then reduces to the same blindness premise. |

So all four reduce to two items, and nothing here supplies either: the ledger (PN), and depth-independence of the self-read (Bl), with A_l(l) ≠ 0 for nonzero gain.

## 5. Priority-B answers

Nothing here is a promising new theorem, so no prediction is proposed. Q1–Q6 of the directive are unchanged from Draft 28's answer: the event does not force a receiver-distinguishable consequence without Bl, Side (here supplied by W2_F) and κ ≠ 0, or in the narrower form, Bl at the step, Side at the siblings and A_l(l) ≠ 0.

## 6. Scratch check (exploratory, not preregistered, disclosed)

`/tmp/sg1/chk.py` (sha256 `4d938fdb…`). Hand values were written first in `/tmp/sg1/HAND.md` (sha256 `02180580…`). Neither file is committed. The check used exact Fractions, seed 20261020, and the address tree with a ternary root and binary below to height 3: 22 addresses and all 17,576 carriers (103,428 leaf cases).

- **Proposition 1(a)–(e):** 6,000 sampled leaf cases on 4 random integer tables in [−3, 3]. PN_e was checked by direct matrix comparison, independently of the formulas.
- **Proposition 2 and its perturbations:** every address pair (l, p), on all contexts.
- **GPT's fork family as an address table:** s ∈ {0, 1/3, 1/2, 1}, on all four subcarriers.

There were 48,288 checks and 0 violations, and every hand value matched on the first run. This is bounded evidence; the general proofs above carry the claims.

## 7. Claim boundary

Earned: Propositions 1–2 and the §3 counterexample, all elementary from Lemma 31.0. Not claimed: any new source of Bl_D^a, (W2_F) or PN; that any vertex performs a read; that a holding is an available record; physical access; occurrence (an accepted empirical input); which outcome is actual. Depth is lineage-address length, not time or distance. Draft 28 and single_event_receiver_gain remain independently accepted conditional results. Native bridge NOT_DERIVED. Broad C3/C4–C6 and physical origin remain OPEN.

# One actual leaf event: a receiver-gain criterion and the precise access obligation

Date: 2026-10-20. Author: proteinfolding-gpt.
Source parent: `aa5aa96c002c181fb2e833f12fcabb15d94c5d6f`.

**Prospective analytical candidate; independent Gemini review pending. Native bridge NOT_DERIVED.** This is an additive continuation of the accepted Drafts 27–28, not a correction to their conditional theorems, a numbered stage, or a numerical campaign. All findings and controls below were developed analytically before the review freeze. Separate acceptance and immutable evidence will be recorded without changing these frozen scientific bytes.

## 1. Positive consequence first

One actual receiver need not obtain the entire distinction exclusively in every carrier for a useful gain to occur. For a fixed P1 leaf event, the pruning ledger relates that receiver's gain to two pre-event responses to a unit placed at the receiver itself. If those responses are nonnegative, either one being positive forces a nonzero formal receiver contrast afterward.

This yields a narrower construction target than Draft 28's all-context exclusive transfer: identify an existing receiver record whose event ledger and two local responses are justified, then show that one response is nonzero and that the record is actually accessible. The argument does not derive those premises. In particular, mathematical distinctness of native grades does not imply that a proposed read map distinguishes them.

The field construction also supplies an exact access test. A post-event own-grade effect has pre-event pullback `h(x_p+x_l)`. The missing native bridge must justify its availability after the event and the complete receiver's blindness before it. This is one concrete effect and one actual event; it does not require full C3 or all-context faithful columns.

## 2. Single-event setting and gain identity

Let W be a finite rooted carrier, l a leaf, p its parent, and Y=W minus {l}. Work over the reals (the identities also hold over the rationals). The P1 map P fixes every retained coordinate other than p and sets

    (Px)_p=x_p+x_l.

Occurrence is accepted as an empirical input. Identifying that actual event with P1 remains a separate typed premise; no occurrence law or fundamental clock is introduced. Compare the same event and source/reference identities in both preparations.

Let F_W:R^W→R^W and F_Y:R^Y→R^Y be linear formal holding maps, with h_v^W(x)=(F_Wx)_v. Impose only this event's ledger relation

    F_Y P = P F_W.                                      (PN_e)

No all-carrier naturality, sibling exchange, cone locality, normalization, or positivity away from the entries named below is required for the theorem. Those properties may be independently available in a candidate application.

Let the declared source pair be x and x+g e_l, g≠0. Specify blindness of the receiver's linear holding at this actual carrier:

    h_p^W(e_l)=0.                                       (B_e)

Linearity makes this independent of background x. This is not yet blindness of the receiver's complete accessible record, and is not Draft 28's chain-comparison condition Bl_D^a.

### Proposition 1: the event's erased direction determines the gain decomposition

Set v=e_l−e_p. Under PN_e there is a scalar beta with

    F_W v=beta v.

Under B_e define t=h_l^W(e_p). Then

    beta=h_p^W(e_p),
    G:=h_p^Y(e_p)=h_l^W(e_l)=beta+t.                     (1)

The receiver's post-event contrast for the declared pair is exactly gG.

**Proof.** P is onto and ker P=span{e_l−e_p}. PN_e gives P F_Wv=F_YPv=0, hence F_Wv=beta v. At coordinate p this reads h_p^W(e_l)−h_p^W(e_p)=−beta, so B_e gives the first identity. At l it reads h_l^W(e_l)−h_l^W(e_p)=beta. Finally P e_l=e_p and the p-coordinate of PN_e gives h_p^Y(e_p)=h_p^W(e_l)+h_l^W(e_l)=h_l^W(e_l). Linearity gives the contrast. QED.

### Corollary 1: two positive entries suffice for a one-event gain criterion

Assume, in addition, only

    h_p^W(e_p)≥0,           h_l^W(e_p)≥0.                (POS_e)

Then beta,t≥0, G≥beta, and

    G>0 iff beta>0 or t>0;
    G=0 iff beta=t=0.                                   (2)

In particular, if F_W(e_l−e_p)≠0, then beta>0 and G>0. Conversely, no gain forces F_W(e_l−e_p)=0 and t=0. Annihilating the erased direction alone does not force no gain.

This sufficient nonzero-kernel-response condition is exactly a nonzero own-unit response h_p^W(e_p)≠0 under PN_e and B_e. It must not be portrayed as an independently earned faithfulness principle. It is sufficient, not necessary: the second branch t>0 may also give gain. If an independently sourced empty-leaf/locality condition supplies t=0, then G=beta and the nonzero-kernel-response condition is equivalent to gain.

No numerical lower bound independent of beta is claimed; no physical units or normalization are derived. A nonzero formal scalar contrast still requires an available effect that distinguishes it. Coarse effects may fail to separate two different scalar values.

## 3. Exact analytical controls

### A. Positive normalized all-prefix family: actual blindness is not chain blindness

Use the three-vertex fork W={p=0,l,c}, with l and c children of p. On every nonempty rooted prefix subcarrier Z, put

    d(Z)=c if c belongs to Z, and p otherwise;
    F_Z=s I_Z+(1−s)e_d(Z) 1_Z^T,       0≤s≤1.           (3)

Here 1_Z^Tx is the total grade. Every coefficient is nonnegative and every column sums to one. For any leaf deletion Q:Z→Z', Qe_d(Z)=e_d(Z') and 1_Z'^TQ=1_Z^T. Consequently F_Z'Q=QF_Z, including both orders of the pruning diamond and their composites. This is a full PN family on the four subcarriers, not merely a pair of unrelated matrices.

On the full fork,

    F_W e_l=s e_l+(1−s)e_c,
    F_W e_p=s e_p+(1−s)e_c.

Thus B_e holds, beta=G=s, t=0, and pruning l gives receiver share s and surviving side share 1−s. At s=0 the receiver remains blind before and after despite positive normalized holdings and the actual nonidentity P1 event. At 0<s<1 there is positive receiver gain, although the unit is not held exclusively at the source or receiver and Draft 28's ET fails for kappa=1.

On the chain {p,l}, instead,

    F_{p,l} e_l=(1−s)e_p+s e_l.

Therefore Bl_1^a holds only at s=1. Blindness at the actual fork cannot be silently substituted for blindness on the comparison chain. The three-vertex no-gain example is minimal among such positive normalized examples: with only p,l, the post-event carrier is {p}, so total normalization forces G=1.

### B. Nonzero kernel response is not necessary

On W={p,l}, in order p,l, take

    F_W=[[0,0],[1,1]],       F_Y=[1],       P=[1,1].

Then PN_e, B_e, positivity and column-total normalization hold. Both units are initially held at l. Here beta=0, t=1, and G=1. The erased relocation contrast is already annihilated by F_W, yet the declared source-presence contrast transfers to p. Distinguish these two contrasts.

### C. Each local sign restriction matters for the stated sufficient implication

On the same two vertices, take

    F_W=[[a,0],[−a,0]],       F_Y=[0],       a∈{−1,1}.

PN_e and B_e hold, beta=a≠0, and G=0. For a=1 only h_l^W(e_p) violates POS_e; for a=−1 only h_p^W(e_p) violates it. Thus a nonzero kernel response without the two stated sign restrictions need not produce gain. These signed controls are not asserted to have positive or unit-normalized total holdings.

## 4. What the existing retention results do and do not supply

Kernel descent already appears in receiver_identification §18.5; the gain ledger appears in §27.0. Proposition 1 is their elementary single-event synthesis, not a new general mathematical principle. Its useful application is the exact criterion (2), its distinction from all-context exclusive transfer, and its small local premise target. No archive-wide novelty is claimed.

The direction v is precisely a distinction the event erases: P e_l=P e_p=e_p. Section 19.1(b) explicitly shows that P1's full classical algebra pullback is not record-compatible when separate leaf and parent grades can collide under addition. RCR or center retention therefore cannot be cited as deriving beta≠0 for this direction. The condition concerns pre-event discrimination of e_l versus e_p by F_W; it is not a claim that P retains their distinction. In contrast, the acquisition pair x and x+g e_l still differs after P by g e_p.

Draft 28 proves exact all-context exclusive transfer from PN plus Bl_D^a and Side_D, and proves their equivalence for that conclusion. Nothing here disproves that result or derives its conditions. This note asks a different, narrower question about nonzero gain in one context. Its hypotheses are a different sufficient set, not a claim that every Draft 28 transfer has beta≠0.

## 5. Actual access: the retained field gives an explicit test

The accepted field construction uses cone totals c_v=Σ_{u≥v}x_u and a comparison-compatible response C with incident-edge coordinates

    y_v=phi_v−phi_parent(v)=a_depth(v)c_v.

The same depth coefficients apply on retained carriers. P1 preserves every retained cone total and every retained depth. Hence it preserves each retained y_v and, with phi_0=0, every retained potential:

    phi_Y(Px)=phi_W(x)|_Y.                              (4)

The proof sums unchanged edge values along the unchanged root-to-vertex path. C and P1 suffice for (4); root shift RS, a constant response coefficient, and nonzero coefficients are unnecessary for this restriction identity. This follows directly from the accepted response form and is consistent with §24.2's C-only preservation argument.

At p, the post-event incident edges are a subset of the pre-event incident edges; only the l edge disappears. Any function of the complete post-event local field is consequently a function of the complete pre-event local field. If the two preparations agree on the probability laws of all actually available pre-event local effects and that available set contains these post-effect pullbacks, they agree on the post-effect laws as well: integrate each common pulled-back effect against the two initial laws. The same argument applies to deterministic preparations.

Complete local-field access before the event is one sufficient condition for this inclusion. Locality alone is not: §§23–24 constrain permitted reads to be local but do not grant every local function. Restricted available algebras can change across the event and remain eligible for acquisition. The generic pullback argument is already familiar from retained_reader_write and center_access_growth; the application below identifies the particular function to trace here.

When the relevant response coefficients are nonzero, the post-event own grade has the following local pre-event representative for nonroot p:

    G_{p,l}(x)=c_p−Σ_{u∈ch_W(p),u≠l}c_u
             =x_p+x_l=x_p(Px).                          (5)

At Genesis replace c_p by the conserved total, if its independent availability is justified. Adding that unchanged datum to both complete local interfaces still gives the inclusion above.

For a fixed existing post-event binary grade effect h, the relevant pullback is h(G_{p,l}), not necessarily the entire number G_{p,l}. A newly accessible contrast requires that this effect was not already available before; complete initial receiver blindness and nonzero post-effect contrast must also be proved. Failure of algebra inclusion or mere unavailability of G_{p,l} is not sufficient. One may already access h(G_{p,l}) without accessing G_{p,l} itself.

### D. A genuine pruning with a blind divergence and a pre-informed complete local field

Take W={0→p→l}, g>0, nonzero a_1,a_2, and compare nonnegative equal-total grades x^0=g e_0 and x^1=g e_l. For x^0 the Genesis-balanced field is zero; for x^1 it is

    (phi_0,phi_p,phi_l)=(0,a_1g,(a_1+a_2)g).

Both initial own grades at p are zero, since the divergence c_p−c_l is zero. After pruning l, the retained field is unchanged and the own grade at p is 0 versus g. However, the incoming gauge-invariant edge value phi_p−phi_0 is already 0 versus a_1g before pruning. Thus a receiver with complete local-field access was already informed. The same field contrast occurs for the original one-location pair 0 versus g e_l, whose totals differ. Equal-total preparation is not required by the theorem and neither pair's native preparability is claimed here.

This is not a contradiction to the selected blind-read theorem. It shows why blindness of its cancelling scalar read cannot establish blindness of a receiver whose other available effects have not been specified. A native restricted record could still implement a real access change; naming its divergence is not a derivation that it does so.

## 6. Exact next native obligation and claim boundary

Start with an existing native receiver-owned record and its actual state-to-record association. For the same preparation pair and actual typed event, establish:

1. The record's event ledger or an independently derived output law. For the single-event linear route, this is PN_e.
2. Complete receiver blindness before the event, together with the two positive local responses and at least one nonzero response if using Corollary 1. Kernel separation may witness the own-unit response, but is not a source-derived axiom.
3. One already justified post-event effect with nonzero contrast and retained source/reference association. For the field/own-grade route, inspect exactly h(x_p+x_l) and show how its availability changes under the native event.

Source-dependent event labels or outcomes could be additional channels, but are outside this fixed same-event calculation and require their own source and access derivation. A probability law can qualify without predicting an individual outcome. None is supplied here as a physical law.

The inspected source-to-record interface and V1172 writer trace do not establish this native association. The latter contains a real computed-field-to-software-output path, while its provenance payload is precomputed; neither is automatically the native receiver's accessible record. This is a bounded finding about the supplied source packet, not a universal absence theorem.

Earned here: the exact conditional single-event identity and controls; the explicit field pullback; a concrete local response and access target. Still unearned: native derivation of the read maps and their ledger, their positive/nonzero responses, actual P1 typing, preparation and binding, physical access and retained readout. Drafts 27–28 remain independently accepted conditional results. Broad C3/C4–C6, physical origin and the native observable milestone remain OPEN. No geometry, energy, dark-matter primitive, fundamental time, new detector or default-branch merge is claimed.

## Sources

The exact immutable source excerpts, full-file identities and byte intervals are in SOURCE_PACKET.json at the stated parent. Claim-bearing sources are receiver_identification_d28_review/RESULT.md §§18.5,19.1,22–24,27 and 33; its accepted STATUS.md; record_consumer_trace/NATIVE_STATE_RECORD_INTERFACE.md; native_record_writer_trace/ASSESSMENT.md; and the earlier retained_reader_write and center_access_growth arguments for prior-work context. Excerpts are dependency evidence, not wholesale re-review of omitted sections or old campaigns.

## 23. The field-to-state association: the receiver's own grade is the only initially blind local read of the retained response field, and the event changes that read by deleting one incident edge (new in draft 17)

Where this sits. proteinfolding-gpt's [NATIVE_STATE_RECORD_INTERFACE.md](../../record_consumer_trace/NATIVE_STATE_RECORD_INTERFACE.md) (`5a0827cf`) found that the composition "localized source → grade pushforward → record" has no source-backed state assignment in its middle interface, and its step 2 asks for an inherited rule assigning native preparations to receiver states, noting that "a directly native classical record could also satisfy the task". Section 22 left one candidate: the receiver's gain is the node-local divergence of a retained response that the event leaves unchanged (Proposition 22.4). This section turns that into a state assignment. The retained response field is v16.22's, the receiver may read it only locally, and the receiver must start uninformed. These three facts determine the receiver's state. It is the receiver's own grade, up to a unit. The assignment is classical and native; no density-matrix encoder, READS entry or copying gate is used. It does not touch the v15.16 quantum sector correspondence (GPT's step 3).

**Setting.** A carrier W (finite rooted tree, Genesis 0), a grade x on W, and nonroot cone totals c_v = C_v(x) for v ≠ 0. The *Genesis-balanced part* of x is x° = x − (Σ x) δ_0. It is a balanced source with the same nonroot cone totals, because δ_0 lies in no nonroot cone. The *retained field* of x is φ = T_W x° ∈ W_W (potentials modulo constants), where T is a response satisfying v16.22's comparison condition C. By v16.22 T2-T3, in edge coordinates d_W φ = M_W c with M_W = diag(a_{depth(e)}). Under (RS), a_k ≡ a_1 (Theorem 22.2), but this section uses RS only where stated. A *local read at a vertex p* is a linear functional f on W_W that depends on φ only through its restriction to the closed neighbourhood N[p] = {p} ∪ {par(p)} ∪ ch(p) in the current carrier. Being defined on W_W, it is invariant under adding constants to φ; that typing is v16.22's, not a choice made here.

**Lemma 23.1 (local reads are incident-flux reads).** For nonroot p, the local reads at p are exactly f = −β a_{k} c_p + Σ_{u ∈ ch(p)} γ_u a_{k+1} c_u with k = depth(p) and free scalars β, γ_u. In grade terms, f = −β a_k x_p + Σ_u (γ_u a_{k+1} − β a_k) c_u, using c_p = x_p + Σ_u c_u. For p = 0, the local reads are f = Σ_{u ∈ ch(0)} γ_u a_1 c_u.
*Proof.* A linear functional of the values φ_q, q ∈ N[p], that vanishes on constants is a combination of the differences φ_q − φ_p, and these are, up to sign, the edge values (dφ) on the edges incident to p. The edge (par(p), p) has depth k and carries a_k c_p. A child edge has depth k + 1 and carries a_{k+1} c_u. The map from W_W to the incident edge values is onto (d_W is an isomorphism), so every combination is attained. At Genesis there is no parent edge. QED.
Reading. Section 17's ownership family (own share a(v) plus shares b(w) of children's cone totals, Theorem 17.1) has the same linear form. Here it appears with no ledger axioms: it is just the set of local reads of the retained field (without 17's W1 normalization and sign condition).

**Theorem 23.2 (initial blindness selects the own grade).** [both directions] Let p be nonroot and the response satisfy C with a_k, a_{k+1} ≠ 0.
(a) A local read f at p is blind to every one-location pair at a strict descendant of p (f(x + g e_z) = f(x) for every z > p and every g) if and only if γ_u a_{k+1} = β a_k for every child u, if and only if f = −β a_k x_p.
(b) Blindness to the one-location pairs at the children of p alone already forces (a). For a uniform rule whose coefficients depend only on the role of the edge (parent or child) and the number of children, blindness on carriers in which every child is a leaf, i.e. on the pairs that a single pruning into p turns into acquisitions, forces (a) on every carrier.
(c) Such a read is blind to every grade except x_p: it ignores ancestors, siblings, the rest of the carrier and the total, and it sees x_p with coefficient −β a_k. So, if it is nontrivial, the receiver's state assigned by the field is its own grade coordinate, up to a unit.
(d) At Genesis the only descendant-blind local read is 0. The total, which x_0 = Σ x − Σ_u c_u needs, is not carried by any potential modulo constants.
(e) Without RS the conclusion of (a) is unchanged, and only the unit a_k depends on depth. With RS, the unit is the same scalar a_1 at every receiver.
*Proof.* (a) A difference at a strict descendant z changes c_p by g, changes c_u by g for the one child u whose cone contains z, and changes no other incident flux. By Lemma 23.1 the read changes by g(γ_u a_{k+1} − β a_k). Taking z = u for each child gives the conditions, and then the grade form of Lemma 23.1 is −β a_k x_p. Conversely, −β a_k x_p does not depend on any x_z with z ≠ p. (b) The first claim is the proof of (a), which uses only z = u. For a uniform rule, γ_u = γ(n) and β = β(n) for a vertex with n children, and the leaf-children case fixes γ(n) a_{k+1} = β(n) a_k for every n. For a depth table with a_{k+1}/a_k varying in k, the rule must be allowed to depend on depth too, and then the same argument applies depth by depth. (c) From the grade form. (d) At Genesis a difference at a child u changes only c_u, so blindness forces every γ_u = 0. (e) The proof uses only diagonality. QED.

**Proposition 23.3 (the event changes the receiver's state without changing the field).** Take the P1 pruning of the leaf l into p = par(l) (forced under CN by Theorem 21.2) and the response a_1 l^{-1} (C + RS). Fix the field's constant by φ_0 = 0.
(a) The retained field is unchanged: φ'_v = φ_v for every v in W ∖ {l}, exactly. The event deletes the vertex l and its edge and nothing else in the field.
(b) If p is nonroot, the descendant-blind read is f = −β a_1 x_p before and f' = −β' a_1 x'_p after (β' is the post-event coefficient of the rule, for n − 1 children), with x'_p = x_p + x_l. For the one-location pair x_l ∈ {0, g}, the read's contrast is 0 before and −β' a_1 g after. It transfers if and only if β' ≠ 0.
(c) The contrast moved from the deleted incident flux into the receiver's read. Before the event the pair differs in the field exactly on the edges of l's lineage, through c_l and every c_v for v an ancestor of l. After it, the pair differs on the same retained edges by the same amounts. The edge (p, l), which carried g, is gone, and the receiver's own read now differs by −β' a_1 g. Nothing is created in the field. Only p's neighbourhood changed.
(d) If p = 0, the pair's fields coincide after the event: the distinction leaves the field and remains only in the total. The field supplies no blind read to Genesis (Theorem 23.2(d)).
*Proof.* (a) The grounded potential is φ_v = a_1 Σ_{e on the path 0 → v} c_e. Proposition 22.4(a) keeps every retained c_e and the total. The path from 0 to a retained v does not pass through the leaf l. (b) By Theorem 23.2 on W and on W ∖ {l}, and Proposition 22.4(b). (c) c_v depends on x_l exactly when l ∈ X_v, and (a). (d) For p = 0, l is a child of Genesis and no retained nonroot cone contains it, so after the event the two Genesis-balanced parts have the same nonroot cone totals. QED.

Reading. This is the missing middle link of GPT's composition for a classical, native record. Native preparation (a grade on the carrier) → retained field (v16.22's response, determined up to one unit under RS) → receiver state (the unique initially blind local read, the own grade) → record (the occupancy algebra and transfer criterion of sections 18-20). The event is the inherited pruning; the field it acts on does not change on any retained vertex; what changes is the receiver's neighbourhood. The receiver becomes informed because the incident edge that carried the source's flux is gone, so the same field, read at the same place with the same local rule, gives a different value. That is the ledger point in field form: a correlation already present in the retained field (on every lineage edge) becomes a node-local state of the receiver by deleting one relation, with no global creation.

**Control 23.4.**
(a) *Without constant invariance.* Reading the grounded value φ_p itself is local in vertex terms, but it equals a_1 Σ_{path} c_e, so it involves the cone totals of every ancestor edge and is already informed by x_l before the event. The W_W typing excludes it.
(b) *Without initial blindness.* A local read with γ_u a_{k+1} ≠ β a_k is pre-informed by (γ_u a_{k+1} − β a_k) g, the field form of section 17's pre-crediting b(l) x_l (Proposition 17.2).
(c) *Without condition C.* For a dense edge-coordinate response (not diagonal), the descendant-blind local reads are generally not the own grade: in the scratch check below, 87 of 188 receiver positions admit no blind read, 97 admit one that is not proportional to x_p, and 4 admit the own grade. Diagonality, which C supplies, is load-bearing.
(d) *Genesis receivers.* For a depth-1 source the receiver is Genesis, and the field gives it nothing (Theorem 23.2(d), Proposition 23.3(d)). The total, an extra datum outside W_W (a boundary flux at Genesis), is needed there. That is a real limit of the field route.

**Earned and assumed.** Earned (general proofs): Lemma 23.1 from v16.22's W_W typing and T2-T3; Theorem 23.2 from Lemma 23.1; Proposition 23.3 from Proposition 22.4 and Theorems 21.2 and 22.2. Assumed: (L) the receiver accesses the retained field only through local reads (the field form of (A1) locality); (B) the read rule is blind to one-location pairs at strict descendants, i.e. the construction's "initially uninformed receiver" required uniformly rather than for one pair; v16.22's condition C; (RS)/(CN) for the event step and the uniform unit; occurrence (existential); availability (A0)-(A3') and (U) for turning the own grade into the occupancy record of sections 18-20; the Genesis-balanced convention for unbalanced grades (any nonroot cone total is insensitive to it); the declared pair; preparability G / N_1(l). Not claimed: that the response field is a physical field, any energy, metric or geometry (depth is lineage-address length, not time or distance), that p performs a read, the v15.16 sector correspondence Tr(P_C σ_x) of GPT's step 3, or which outcome is actual. Native bridge: NOT_DERIVED. No milestone.

**Novelty, stated plainly.** Mathematically elementary: the node divergence is the standard local, constant-invariant functional of a potential on a graph (Kirchhoff's current law), and its insensitivity to sources downstream of the node is standard tree-Green-function bookkeeping. What is new for UQCF: GPT's missing field-to-state association is supplied for a directly native classical record. The receiver's state is derived as the only initially blind local read of the inherited response field, rather than chosen. Section 17's ownership family reappears as the space of local field reads. The event changes the receiver's state with the retained field literally unchanged, by an incidence deletion. The Genesis limitation is identified exactly. No measurement model, decoherence, einselection or quantum Darwinism content is claimed.

**Scratch check (exploratory, not preregistered, disclosed).** `/tmp/rid20/chk23.py` (exact Fractions; seed 20261019; sha256 `8b3f3ce9…`; not committed). Universe: every rooted tree with 1 to 7 vertices up to rooted isomorphism (85 carriers). The field is computed independently of the cone-total formula, by solving the grounded weighted Laplacian (edge conductance 1/a_depth) for the Genesis-balanced part. Results: for each of three depth tables (a ≡ 1, a ≡ 3, T_depth a_k = k), the descendant-blind local reads (constant-invariant functionals on N[p]) form a one-dimensional space at each of the 441 nonroot (carrier, p) positions. Each read vanishes on every e_z with z ≠ p and not on e_p. At Genesis the space is 0 on all 85 carriers. Event: every leaf of every carrier, three values of g, random rational backgrounds (1,512 field solves): the post-event grounded field equals the pre-event field on every retained vertex. The divergence read equals x_p before and x'_p after, its contrast is 0 before and g after for nonroot p, and for Genesis receivers the two post-event fields coincide. Control 23.4(c): 188 receiver positions with a dense random edge-coordinate response, with (dimension, own-grade) counts (0, no) 87, (1, no) 97, (1, yes) 4. Total 8,139 checks, 0 violations.

**Next.** Freeze section 23 with a preregistered universe (carriers up to 7 or 8 vertices, the local-read dimension at every position and depth table, the Genesis zero, the event field identity and contrast over every leaf, and the dense-response control) and an independent producer and checker, then Gemini. Constructive: the Genesis gap, whether the total is carried by an inherited boundary datum; and whether the uniform blindness premise (B) follows from the event typing itself, since CN puts every strict descendant's grade in the receiver's subtree and so outside what any pruning above p can move.

## 26. Every vertex is a possible receiver: the read ledger with cone-local reads gives the field family, and leaf blindness then forces own-grade reads everywhere (new in draft 20)

Where this sits. Sections 23-25 built the receiver's read out of v16.22's retained field. They used local field access (L), a uniform rule, condition C, the read ledger (PN) and root-shift premises ((RS), (RS_F), (CN_F)). Section 25 also assumed that Genesis's read has the form "field read plus a linear datum". Two questions were left. (i) Does (CN_F) follow from CN for the step together with (PN), or from some naturality that the read ledger forces? (ii) Can the form assumed for Genesis's read be derived? This section drops the field, locality, uniformity, C and every assumption about Genesis, and asks what the read ledger alone fixes for arbitrary linear read maps on grades. (PN) alone leaves a lower-triangular depth matrix (Proposition 26.1). If each vertex reads only its own relative view (cone-local reads), the result is exactly the family of sections 24-25, Genesis datum included (Proposition 26.2). That answers (ii). Adding blindness along the record's climb, or the one-vertex root shift, then forces F̂ = κ id (Theorem 26.3). So (CN_F) follows from (PN) plus its own one-vertex instance, but not from CN for the step (Proposition 26.4). That answers (i). This is a positive construction. It uses no positivity, no inverse axiom and no metric. The P1 step is the one forced under CN (Theorem 21.2), and CN is still assumed.

**Setting.** The carriers W are all finite rooted trees, with Genesis 0, as in sections 21-25. Grades are x ∈ F^W, and P = P_{W, W∖{l}} is the P1 step of a single pruning. A *read map* is a family of linear maps F̂_W : F^W → F^W, one per carrier, invariant under rooted isomorphisms; F̂_W(x)_v is the read at v. No locality, uniformity, field, response or Genesis form is assumed. The cone coordinates of Proposition 22.3 are x ↦ (c_v(x))_{v ∈ W}, with c_0 = Σ x and c_v the cone total. Applied to a read vector r they give its cone read sums s_v(r) = Σ_{t ∈ X_v} r_t. Write w ≤ v for "w is an ancestor of v or v itself". Conditions:
- (PN) *The read ledger.* At every single pruning, F̂_Y(P x) = P F̂_W(x). This is section 24's (PN), the descent square of section 18.5(a)(ii) written for reads.
- (S) *Cone-local reads.* F̂_W(x)_v depends only on x restricted to X_v (v reads only its own relative view, the retained history visible from v; section 22). Equivalently, a unit at z is read only by the vertices v ≤ z. (S_leaf) is the same condition for units at leaves only.
- (W2_F) *Zero-extension naturality for reads.* F̂_{X'} ∘ I = I ∘ F̂_X for every prefix-closed X ⊆ X', with I the FCV P2 zero extension. This is section 17's (W2) and section 21's (NI) square, written for reads. The morphism I is inherited; requiring reads to commute with it is a locality requirement.
- (C_climb) *Climb blindness.* For every leaf a of every carrier, every strict ancestor of a reads 0 on δ_a. Each later holder on the record's climb (sections 12 and 14) is uninformed of the leaf's unit before it receives it. (C_recv) is the same condition for v = par(a) only, which is the read form of Theorem 17.3(iii).
- (Z) *Leaf-point blindness.* F̂_W(δ_a)_v = 0 for every leaf a ≠ 0 and every v ≠ a. By definition (Z) is (S_leaf) together with (C_climb). It is (CN_F) at the one-vertex cones X_a = {a}, up to the coefficient.
- (G⁺) *Genesis as apex of its one-vertex extension.* Let W⁺ be W with a new Genesis attached above the old one, and ι : F^W → F^{W⁺} zero extension. (G⁺) requires F̂_{W⁺} ∘ ι = ι ∘ F̂_W. This is (CN_F) at the cone of the only child of Genesis in W⁺.
- (CN_F) as in section 25, imposed on the whole read map, with no form assumed for any read.

**Proposition 26.1 (the read ledger alone leaves a lower-triangular depth matrix).** [both directions] A read map satisfies (PN) if and only if there is a table ν(k, j), 0 ≤ j ≤ k, such that on every carrier

    s_v(F̂_W(x)) = Σ_{w ≤ v} ν(depth v, depth w) c_w(x)   for every v ∈ W,     (26.1)

where the term w = 0 is ν(depth v, 0) Σ x. In vertex terms, F̂_W(x)_v = s_v − Σ_{u ∈ ch(v)} s_u. The table is free otherwise. On carriers with at most N vertices, the (PN) solution space has dimension N(N + 1)/2. The total read is ν(0, 0) Σ x, which is Proposition 25.1 again.
*Proof.* By Proposition 22.3, P acts on every vector, grade or read, by deleting the coordinate c_l and keeping the others. Write S_W for F̂_W in cone coordinates. Then (PN) says del_l S_W = S_Y del_l at every pruning, that is: (i) S_W[v, l] = 0 for every retained v; and (ii) S_W[v, w] = S_Y[v, w] for retained v and w. Repeated use of (ii) gives S_W[v, w] = S_Z[v, w], where Z is the smallest prefix-closed set containing v and w (prune every other leaf). If w ≤ v, Z is the chain to v, so S_Z[v, w] depends only on the two depths, by isomorphism invariance. Otherwise w is a leaf of Z other than v, and (i) gives 0. Conversely, the entries ν(k_v, k_w) 1[w ≤ v] satisfy (i), because a leaf is not an ancestor of any other vertex, and (ii), because pruning a leaf changes no depth and no ancestry among retained vertices. For the dimension, every pair 0 ≤ j ≤ k ≤ N − 1 occurs on the N-vertex chain. QED.
Reading. This is the read analogue of Proposition 21.1 and of v16.22's a_k. With no locality at all, the inherited event leaves a depth-indexed residual, here a lower-triangular matrix. The off-diagonal entries are reads of units sitting in other branches (Control 26.5(a)).

**Proposition 26.2 (cone-local reads are exactly the field family, and the Genesis form is derived).** [all directions] Under (PN), the following are equivalent:
(a) (S);
(b) (S_leaf);
(c) ν is diagonal, ν(k, j) = 0 for j < k;
(d) with μ_k := −ν(k, k) for k ≥ 1 and θ := ν(0, 0), for every carrier,

    F̂_W(x)_v = −μ_k x_v + (μ_{k+1} − μ_k) Σ_{u ∈ ch(v)} c_u  (v ≠ 0, k = depth v),    F̂_W(x)_0 = μ_1 Σ_{u ∈ ch(0)} c_u + θ Σ x.     (26.2)

(e) (W2_F).

(26.2) is the composite of Theorem 24.3(a) together with section 25's Genesis datum λ = θ Σ x (the form of Proposition 25.1). v16.22's field realizes every member: for any response with C and every a_k ≠ 0, take section 24's rule (iv) with m_k = μ_k / a_k and add λ = θ Σ x. So the family that sections 23-25 obtained from (L), uniformity, C and the read ledger also follows from the read ledger and cone-locality alone. Genesis's read "field read plus a multiple of the total" is then a consequence and no longer an assumed form. Genesis is the vertex whose cone is the whole carrier, and the total is that cone's coordinate. Section 17's ownership family (17.1) with depth-indexed shares b_k is the diagonal subfamily ν(k, k) = 1 − Σ_{j ≤ k} b_j, ν(0, 0) = 1 (W1).
*Proof.* (c) ⇒ (a): with ν diagonal, s_v = ν(k, k) c_v depends only on x restricted to X_v, and so do the s_u of v's children and hence s_v − Σ s_u. (a) ⇒ (b) is immediate. (b) ⇒ (c): put A(k, m) = Σ_{j ≤ m} ν(k, j). Let v be a leaf of depth k, and let z be a leaf attached to v's ancestor of depth m < k, so z is not below v. The cone totals of δ_z are 1 exactly at the vertices w ≤ z, so F̂(δ_z)_v = s_v = A(k, m). (S_leaf) gives A(k, m) = 0 for every m < k, hence ν(k, j) = 0 for j < k. (c) ⇔ (d): with ν diagonal, F̂_v = ν(k, k) c_v − ν(k+1, k+1) Σ_u c_u and c_v = x_v + Σ_u c_u; at Genesis, F̂_0 = θ Σ x − ν(1, 1) Σ_u c_u. (e) ⇒ (a) is Lemma 17.0's argument: F̂_W(δ_z) = I F̂_{[0,z]}(δ_z) is supported on the chain [0, z], whose vertices are exactly the v ≤ z. (c) ⇒ (e): for x supported in X, c_v(I x) = c_v(x) for v ∈ X, c_v(I x) = 0 for v ∉ X, and the children of v ∈ X that are not in X have zero cone, so with ν diagonal the reads agree on X and vanish outside it. Realization is Theorem 24.3(a) with (25.1). For section 17, a unit at z ∈ X_v is held inside X_v with total share a(z) + Σ_{v < w ≤ z} b(w) = 1 − Σ_{0 < w ≤ v} b(w). QED.

**Theorem 26.3 (leaf blindness forces own-grade reads everywhere; (CN_F) is a consequence).** [all directions] For a read map satisfying (PN), the following are equivalent:
(a) (Z);
(b) (S) and (C_climb);
(c) (S) and (C_recv);
(d) (S) and (G⁺);
(e) (CN_F) at every cone;
(f) ν = κ I, that is, F̂_W = κ id on every carrier, with κ = F̂_{{0}}(1).
In the field family (26.2) these conditions say μ_k ≡ μ and θ = −μ (κ = −μ). That is Theorem 25.2(c), now with no form assumed for Genesis's read.
*Proof.* (a) ⇒ (f), by leaf attachment. Let Y be a carrier and p ∈ Y, and let W be Y with a new leaf l attached below p. By (Z), F̂_W(δ_l) = κ_{W,l} δ_l. (PN) at the pruning W → Y with x = δ_l gives F̂_Y(δ_p) = P F̂_W(δ_l) = κ_{W,l} δ_p. So every F̂_Y is diagonal. (PN) at any pruning with x = δ_v keeps the diagonal entry of every retained v, and with x = δ_l it makes the receiver's entry equal to the leaf's. Prune down to {0}: every entry equals F̂_{{0}}(1) = κ (the argument of Proposition 25.1). (f) ⇒ (a)-(e): κ id is diagonal and commutes with P, ι and every j_a. (b) ⇒ (c) is immediate. (c) ⇒ (f): ν is diagonal by Proposition 26.2. For a leaf a of depth d, F̂(δ_a)_{par(a)} = ν(d−1, d−1) − ν(d, d), so (C_recv) makes the diagonal constant. (d) ⇒ (f): with ν diagonal, compare v's read in W, at depth k ≥ 1, with its read in W⁺, at depth k + 1. At x = δ_v this gives ν(k, k) = ν(k+1, k+1). The old Genesis is a depth-1 vertex of W⁺, and it reads ν(1, 1) Σ x − ν(2, 2) Σ_u c_u there and θ Σ x − ν(1, 1) Σ_u c_u in W, so θ = ν(1, 1) = ν(2, 2). (e) ⇒ (a): (CN_F) at a one-vertex cone X_a = {a} says F̂_W(δ_a) = j_a F̂_{{a}}(1) ∈ F δ_a. QED.
Reading. Every vertex, Genesis included, is the receiver of a possible pruning: attach a leaf to it. The ledger says that at that pruning the receiver's read gains exactly what the leaf read. Leaf-point blindness says that only the leaf read the leaf's unit. So a unit sitting at the receiver is read as κ there and as 0 everywhere else. The construction's starting condition, an initially uninformed receiver, imposed at leaves and transported by the ledger, becomes own-grade reading at every vertex. The argument uses the larger carrier and its pruning. It does not use an append event, N_1(l) or the occurrence of the larger carrier, only that the read map is defined on every carrier, as in sections 21-25. In a finite universe the argument stops one vertex short (Control 26.5(c)).

**Proposition 26.4 (what is and is not derived about the read root shift).**
(a) *Target (i), positive.* (CN_F) follows from (PN) together with its own one-vertex instance (Z) (Theorem 26.3, (a) ⇔ (e)). Within the cone-local class (S), one apex square per carrier, (G⁺), is already enough.
(b) *Target (i), negative.* CN for the step together with (PN) does not imply (Z), (S), (C_recv) or (CN_F). The P1 step satisfies CN (Theorem 21.2(b)), and each of the following witnesses satisfies (PN) for it. The Genesis-dump read F̂_W(x) = (Σ x) δ_0 (ν = E_00) satisfies (S) and fails (C_recv) at Genesis. Section 24's field read with no Genesis datum (μ ≡ 1, λ = 0) satisfies (S) and fails at Genesis (Theorem 25.2(d)). T_depth with m ≡ 1 (μ_k = k) satisfies (S) and fails (C_climb) at every nonroot ancestor. ν = I + E_20 − E_21 satisfies (C_climb) and fails (S) (Control 26.5(a)). The reason is that CN constrains the step maps, and (PN) already uses the step that CN forces; no read datum enters either condition. So the read root shift is a separate instance of the same morphism type, as Proposition 25.4 found for (RS_F).
(c) *Against earlier sections.* Given (PN), (CN_F) is equivalent to (Z). So section 25's root-shift premise for reads and the construction's starting condition "an initially uninformed receiver" are the same premise, when the latter is required at the receiver of every leaf pruning, along its climb, and at non-ancestors (lineage locality). On the field family, (Z) is μ constant with θ = −μ, which is (B) at nonroot receivers (Theorem 24.3(b)) plus Genesis blindness (Proposition 24.4(b)); sections 24-25 already showed this, and it is not new. What is new: the general class (no (L), no uniformity, no C, no field, no Genesis form); the residual of Proposition 26.1; the fact that (S) alone yields the field family with its Genesis datum (Proposition 26.2), a form section 25 assumed; and the fact that, given (S), blindness at the receiver alone (C_recv) suffices. Relative to section 17: Theorem 17.3 ((W1), (W2), (W4) and receiver blindness force the identity) is the ownership version. Under (PN), (S) is equivalent to (W2_F) (Proposition 26.2(e)). So Theorem 26.3(c), in the form (PN) + (W2_F) + (C_recv) ⇒ κ id, is Theorem 17.3 for reads with (W1) and (W4) replaced by (PN): the normalization and sign of (W1) are not used, and the unit κ stays free where (W1) fixed it to 1. That route is not new. (b) *No constraint.* (O3-leaf) alone, with or without (PN), imposes no linear condition on an arbitrary read map F̂. In particular the off-diagonal witness ν = I + E_20 − E_21 of Lemma 27.1 satisfies (PN) and (O3-leaf) and fails (E0)/(S_L).
(c) *Bridge restates (S_L).* The natural bridge premise (RV_l): "the leaf's read F̂_W(·)_l is a linear functional of the O3 coordinates of X_l" means F̂_W(x)_l = α_l c_l(x) = α_l x_l, which is exactly (S_L) at l. Under (PN), (RV_l) for every leaf ⇔ (S_L) ⇔ (E0) ⇔ (W2_1) ⇔ (S) (Proposition 27.2). So sourcing (E0) from O3 via (RV) does not discharge (E0); it assumes leaf-locality under another name.
*Proof.* (a) is O3 at a singleton cone. (b): O3-leaf does not mention F̂; the witness is Lemma 27.1 and Proposition 27.4(c). (c): c_l = x_l, so a functional of c_l is a multiple of x_l, which is (S_L); the equivalences are Proposition 27.2. QED.

**Proposition 28.2 (morphism-style depth-shift on the diagonal family).** Assume (PN) + (S_L), so ν is diagonal with free entries ν(k, k) for k = 0, 1, … . Let W⁺ be W with a new Genesis attached above the old root, and ι the zero extension of grades (the (G⁺) setup of section 26). Write ν and ν⁺ for the depth tables of F̂_W and F̂_{W⁺}.
(a) *(G⁺) on the diagonal.* (G⁺), i.e. F̂_{W⁺} ∘ ι = ι ∘ F̂_W for every W, holds for the whole cone-local family if and only if ν(k, k) = ν(k+1, k+1) for every k ≥ 0 and θ = ν(0, 0) matches in the usual way (the calculation of Theorem 26.3(d)). In particular (G⁺) forces the diagonal constant, hence F̂ = κ id.
(b) *Depth-shift as adjacent equality for all depths.* Define (DS) to be the family of equalities ν(k, k) = ν(k+1, k+1) for every k ≥ 0 (one structural comparison of W with W⁺ at every depth). Then on the cone-local class, (DS) ⇔ (G⁺).
(c) *Propagation from one equality is not a morphism.* The algebraic constraint (DS_prop): "if ν(d, d) = ν(d+1, d+1) for some d, then ν is constant on all depths" forces κ id from (CL_1) alone, but it is not the naturality of any inherited inclusion or pruning; it is a global constraint on the depth table and is not supplied by O3, CN or (PN).
*Proof.* (a) is the (d) ⇒ (f) direction of Theorem 26.3, restricted to diagonal ν. (b) is the same calculation read as a definition of (DS). (c): (DS_prop) mentions no carrier morphism; (PN) and O3 constrain how tables transform under pruning and restriction, not whether one accidental equality propagates. QED.

The draft-22 statement listed climbs of every depth among unconditional equivalents of (G⁺). The zero read F̂ = 0 on every carrier is a counterexample: it satisfies (PN), (S_L), (G⁺) and (DS), yet it separates no pair and fails every (CL_D), since (CL_D) includes acquisition.] Under (PN) + (S_L), on the class of all finite carriers:
(a) (G⁺) ⇔ (DS) ⇔ F̂ = κ id for some scalar κ, with κ = 0 allowed.
(b) With κ ≠ 0 added: ((G⁺) and κ ≠ 0) ⇔ ((DS) and κ ≠ 0) ⇔ (CL_D) for every D ≥ 1 ⇔ ((CL_1) and (DS)).
(c) (CL_D) for one fixed D together with (G⁺) or (DS): the climb is redundant for the identity conclusion. It only names the common unit as the climb's gain.
In this general read class κ need not be positive; section 29's (POS) makes a nonzero unit positive. Algebraic compatibility with climb acquisitions does not establish that those climbs physically occur. Within the comparison class of Proposition 28.2 (the full apex comparisons W → W⁺ with zero extension), no depth-shift short of (G⁺)/(DS) closes Proposition 27.4(a)'s horizon from one finite climb. No classification of other morphism systems is claimed.
*Proof.* (a) (G⁺) ⇔ (DS) is Proposition 28.2(b). (DS) says the diagonal of ν is constant, which under (S_L) is F̂ = κ id; conversely κ id satisfies (G⁺) and (DS) for every κ, 0 included. (b) For each depth k, (CL_k) with acquisition forces ν(k, k) = ν(k − 1, k − 1) = … = κ ≠ 0 (Theorem 27.3); as D runs through all depths the diagonal is constant, so F̂ = κ id with κ ≠ 0, which gives (G⁺) and (DS) by (a). Conversely κ id with κ ≠ 0 gives blindness before, and acquisition κ g after, every step of every climb. For the last equivalence, (DS) gives κ id by (a), and the acquisition in (CL_1) gives κ ≠ 0; the converse is immediate. (c) (G⁺) alone already forces κ id, so adding (CL_D) does not weaken the structural premise. QED.

**Control 28.4.**
(a) *O3 does not kill the ker-P defect.* The witness ν = I + E_20 − E_21 satisfies (PN) and (O3-leaf) and fails (S_L) at the depth-2 leaf (read of δ_0 equals 1).
(b) *(CL_1) alone leaves the horizon.* Under (PN) + (S_L) + (CL_1), dimension is N − 1 on carriers with at most N vertices (Proposition 27.4(a)); the free directions are ν(k, k) for k ≥ 2.

Assumed: (PN); (S_L)/(E0); for the identity conclusion, either (G⁺)/(DS) or climbs of every depth; CN for the step. ## 31. Shape-uniformity is used only as sibling exchange at the climb's own forks: with address-dependent reads, every climb unit is read faithfully (new in draft 25)

Where this sits. Section 30 left one assumption beyond the inherited class: one read rule across the comb's rooted subtrees, that is, isomorphism invariance of the reads between different carriers. If a read law is by definition a function of the carrier up to rooted isomorphism, that holds automatically and section 30 applies as it stands. This section treats the weaker case in which the read law may depend on lineage addresses, so that each lineage may have its own rule, and asks how much uniformity the construction actually uses. (a) A single realized pruning history cannot supply it. Its carriers strictly decrease in size, so no two are isomorphic, and along one history a leaf may hold any fraction t ∈ [0, κ] of its receiver's unit at every step (Remark 31.4). (b) On the address class, (PN) still reduces the reads to one table, now indexed by addresses (Lemma 31.0). (c) (PN), (POS) and blindness along one addressed climb clean every side branch off the climb. The only freedom left in the climb's columns is a bottleneck leak t_m through the climb's own next vertex, which bounds every descendant's share of the unit (Theorem 31.1; [D26]). (d) Exchange symmetry of the two children of each climb vertex, on one fork carrier per depth (D automorphisms of single carriers in all), removes that leak. Every climb unit is then read faithfully, F̂_W e_{a_m} = κ e_{a_m}, on every carrier that contains it, whatever else the carrier contains (Theorem 31.2). So for steps above the horizon the transfer is context-independent (Corollary 31.3). The transfer is the same as before. At the step that prunes a_d, the receiver a_{d−1} gains κ g, which is exactly the leaf's holding, and the total holding is conserved (Lemma 27.0).

**Setting.** 𝒜 is a rooted tree of lineage addresses with Genesis 0 as its root. Carriers are the finite rooted subtrees W of 𝒜, that is, vertex sets containing 0 and the parent of each of their nonroot vertices. This class is closed under leaf deletion (Lemma 30.0) and contains every chain [0, v] and every fork. Each carrier has a linear read map F̂_W: F^W → F^W. **No invariance between different carriers is assumed.** (PN) and (POS) are as in section 29, for every leaf pruning of every carrier. Fix one climb a_0 = 0, a_1, …, a_D, with a_d a child of a_{d−1}. (Bl_D^a) is blindness along this addressed climb: at the step that prunes a_d from the chain [0, a_d], the receiver a_{d−1} reads the same on x and x + g e_{a_d}. Assume each a_m with m ≤ D − 1 has a second child address u_m ≠ a_{m+1}, and let F_m = [0, a_m] ∪ {a_{m+1}, u_m} be the fork carrier. (SX_m), sibling exchange on F_m, is F̂_{F_m} σ_m = σ_m F̂_{F_m}, where σ_m swaps a_{m+1} and u_m. This is invariance under one automorphism of one carrier, not a comparison of two carriers. Notation: v ∧ z is the deepest common ancestor of v and z. For w an ancestor-or-self of v, A_v(w) = Σ_{w′ ≤ w} ν_v(w′), the sum running over the ancestors-or-self w′ of w. κ := A_0(0).

**Lemma 31.0 (address table).** (PN) holds on the address class if and only if there are numbers ν_v(w), one for each address v and each ancestor-or-self w of v and independent of the carrier, such that s_v = Σ_{w ≤ v} ν_v(w) c_w on every carrier containing v. The holding of v under the unit grade e_z is then h_v(e_z) = A_v(v ∧ z) − Σ_{u ∈ ch_W(v)} A_u(u ∧ z).
*Proof.* This is Lemma 29.0 without its last use of isomorphism invariance. Write s_v = Σ_w M_W(v, w) c_w. Deleting leaves down to the subtree spanned by the paths to v and w gives M_W(v, w) = 0 unless w ≤ v, and M_W(v, w) = M_{[0,v]}(v, w) otherwise. For the holding formula, s_v(e_z) = Σ_{w ≤ v, w ≤ z} ν_v(w) = A_v(v ∧ z) and F̂(x)_v = s_v − Σ_{children} s_u. The converse is the computation of Proposition 26.1. QED.

**Theorem 31.1 (without uniformity, the side branches are clean and the climb's next vertex may leak).** Assume (PN), (POS) and (Bl_D^a) on the address class. Then:
(a) A_{a_d}(a_d) = κ ≥ 0 for 0 ≤ d ≤ D.
(b) *Side branches are clean.* For m ≤ D − 1, every child u ≠ a_{m+1} of a_m and every descendant c of u (u included), A_c(a_m) = 0.
(c) *The only freedom is along the climb.* For m ≤ D − 1 and every descendant c of a_{m+1} with parent c′ ≠ a_m, 0 ≤ A_c(a_m) ≤ A_{c′}(a_m). Hence 0 ≤ A_c(a_m) ≤ t_m := A_{a_{m+1}}(a_m) ≤ κ.
(d) *Every leak occurs.* For 0 < κ, m ≤ D − 1 and t ∈ [0, κ], let A_v(w) = κ [w = v] (the κ id table), except A_{a_{m+1}}(a_m) = t and A_c(c) = κ − t for every c strictly below a_m and not at or below a_{m+1}. This table satisfies (PN), (POS) and (Bl_D^a), with acquisition κ g at every climb step. On the chain [0, a_{m+1}], the leaf a_{m+1} reads t x_{a_m}, so (E0) fails at the climb's own next vertex when t > 0. On F_m, a_{m+1} holds t of e_{a_m} while u_m holds 0, so (SX_m) fails for t > 0.
*Proof.* (a) This is Step 1 of Theorem 29.1. On [0, a_d], h_{a_{d−1}}(e_{a_d}) = A_{a_{d−1}}(a_{d−1}) − A_{a_d}(a_d), and (POS) on {0} gives κ ≥ 0. (b) On the fork [0, a_m] ∪ {a_{m+1}, u} with x = e_{a_{m+1}}, the vertex u holds A_u(a_m), and a_m holds A_{a_m}(a_m) − A_{a_{m+1}}(a_{m+1}) − A_u(a_m) = −A_u(a_m) by (a), since m + 1 ≤ D. (POS) at both gives A_u(a_m) = 0. For descendants, on the chain [0, c] with x = e_{a_m}, the parent c′ holds A_{c′}(a_m) − A_c(a_m) and c holds A_c(a_m). So 0 ≤ A_c(a_m) ≤ A_{c′}(a_m), and induction from u gives 0. (c) The same chain inequality, with induction from a_{m+1}. On [0, a_{m+1}] with x = e_{a_m}, a_m holds κ − t_m ≥ 0, and a_{m+1} holds t_m ≥ 0. (d) Only the holdings of a_m, of a_{m+1} and of the vertices in the side subtrees of a_m change. For v in a side subtree, both A_v(v ∧ z) and the children's entries are (κ − t) times the corresponding indicator, so h_v(e_z) = (κ − t)[z = v] ≥ 0. For v = a_{m+1}, the children u satisfy A_u(a_m) = 0, so h_v(e_z) = κ [z = a_{m+1}] + t [a_{m+1} ∧ z = a_m] ≥ 0. For v = a_m: if z = a_m, h = κ − t [a_{m+1} ∈ W] ≥ 0. If z lies at or below a_{m+1}, h = κ − κ = 0. If z lies in a side subtree, h = κ − (κ − t) − t [a_{m+1} ∈ W] ≥ 0. An ancestor a_i of a_m holds κ − κ = 0 of every unit below a_{i+1}, because A_{a_{i+1}}(a_{i+1}) = κ is unchanged. Every other holding keeps its κ id value. (Bl_D^a) holds because the climb's diagonal entries are unchanged, (PN) holds by Lemma 31.0, and the gain at every step is the leaf's holding κ (Lemma 27.0). On F_m with x = e_{a_m}: h_{a_{m+1}} = t and h_{u_m} = A_{u_m}(a_m) = 0. QED.

**Theorem 31.2 (sibling exchange at the climb's forks makes every climb unit faithful).** Assume (PN), (POS), (Bl_D^a) and (SX_m) for 0 ≤ m ≤ D − 1. Then t_m = 0 and A_{u_m}(u_m) = κ for every m ≤ D − 1, and on every carrier W that contains a_m (m ≤ D − 1),
F̂_W e_{a_m} = κ e_{a_m}.
Every vertex of every such carrier reads nothing of a climb unit except the unit's own address, which reads it in the common unit κ.
*Proof.* σ_m fixes a_m. So (SX_m) applied to x = e_{a_m} gives h_{a_{m+1}}(e_{a_m}) = h_{u_m}(e_{a_m}) on F_m, that is, t_m = A_{u_m}(a_m) = 0 by Theorem 31.1(b). Then A_c(a_m) = 0 for every c strictly below a_m, by Theorem 31.1(b)-(c). Applied to x = e_{a_{m+1}}, (SX_m) gives A_{u_m}(u_m) = h_{u_m}(e_{u_m}) = h_{a_{m+1}}(e_{a_{m+1}}) = κ. Now let W contain a_m, and let v ∈ W. If v = a_m, then h_v = κ − Σ_u A_u(a_m) = κ. If v lies strictly below a_m, every term of h_v is a column-a_m entry strictly below a_m, so h_v = 0. If v = a_i with i < m, then a_{i+1} ∈ W because W is rooted, and h_v = A_{a_i}(a_i) − A_{a_{i+1}}(a_{i+1}) − Σ_{u ≠ a_{i+1}} A_u(a_i) = κ − κ − 0 = 0, since i + 1 ≤ D. If v is incomparable with a_m, then v ∧ a_m = a_i for some i < m and v lies at or below a child u ≠ a_{i+1} of a_i, so v and its children have column-a_i entries 0 by Theorem 31.1(b), and h_v = 0. QED.

**Corollary 31.3 (a context-independent transfer above the horizon).** Under the premises of Theorem 31.2, let 1 ≤ d ≤ D − 1, and let W be any carrier in which a_d is a leaf with parent a_{d−1}. Prune a_d (the P1 step, Y = W − a_d). Before the step, F̂_W(g e_{a_d}) = κ g e_{a_d}: the receiver a_{d−1} and every other vertex read nothing of the distinction, and only its own address holds it. After the step, F̂_Y(P g e_{a_d}) = F̂_Y(g e_{a_{d−1}}) = κ g e_{a_{d−1}}: the receiver holds exactly κ g, and every other vertex still holds nothing of it. The total holding κ g is conserved. This holds in every carrier containing the climb's lineage, not only on the chain where blindness was imposed. For d = D, the before-step statement holds on the chain [0, a_D] by (Bl_D^a), but not in every context, because column a_D is not controlled (horizon).
*Proof.* Theorem 31.2 at m = d and at m = d − 1, together with P e_{a_d} = e_{a_{d−1}} (CN). QED.

**Remark 31.4 (one realized history supplies no uniformity).** Let W_0 ⊃ W_1 ⊃ … be a realized pruning history, one leaf per step. Sizes strictly decrease, so no two of its carriers are isomorphic, and invariance between isomorphic carriers says nothing inside it. Suppose the maps on the history's carriers are otherwise free. Then (PN) at the step from W_i to W_{i+1} (leaf l, receiver p) determines every row of F̂_{W_i} except that the l-row and the p-row are fixed only in their sum. If F̂_{W_{i+1}} = κ id, then (POS) and the receiver's blindness leave exactly F̂_{W_i} = κ id + t (E_{lp} − E_{pp}) with t ∈ [0, κ]: the leaf holds t of its receiver's unit. So a history's own steps cannot decide (E0). The comparison has to come from other configurations in the class (sections 29-30) or from symmetry within one carrier (this section).
*Proof.* Put φ(x) = (F̂_{W_i} x)_l and ψ(x) = (F̂_{W_{i+1}} P x)_p. Then (F̂_{W_i} x)_p = ψ(x) − φ(x), and every other row is a row of F̂_{W_{i+1}} P. (POS) gives 0 ≤ φ(e_v) ≤ ψ(e_v) = κ [v ∈ {p, l}]. Blindness gives φ(e_l) = ψ(e_l) = κ. Only φ(e_p) = t ∈ [0, κ] remains free. QED.

Reading. Section 30 said that what the positivity route needs beyond the inherited class is one read rule across the comb's rooted subtrees. This section shows that even this is more than is used. Let the read law depend on lineage addresses. Positivity, the ledger and one blind climb already clean every lineage that branches off the climb. This is the same sandwich as in section 29: the blind receiver and its empty side child together hold zero of the next climb unit. What remains is one bottleneck number per depth, t_m, the share of a climb vertex's unit held by the climb's own next vertex; vertices below it may share part of t_m, never more ([D26](iii)). This is the one place where the empty-child comparison cannot reach, because the next vertex is not empty there. A single symmetry of a single carrier, exchanging the climb's next vertex with its empty sibling, sets t_m = 0. With those D exchanges, every climb unit is held only at its own address in every carrier, and the receiver of every step above the horizon is blind before and gains exactly κ g after, whatever else is present. The symmetry used is the structural indistinguishability of two siblings within one configuration. It is weaker than requiring two different configurations to be read by the same rule.

**Earned and assumed.** Earned (general proofs): Lemma 31.0 from (PN) and leaf deletion on the address class; Theorem 31.1 from (POS) on chains and forks, with an explicit extremal family; Theorem 31.2 and Corollary 31.3 from one sibling exchange per depth; Remark 31.4 by direct computation. Assumed: linear reads, one map per carrier; (PN); (POS); (Bl_D^a) along one addressed climb (the construction's uninformed receiver), with acquisition for κ > 0; a second child address at each climb vertex above the horizon; (SX_m) for m ≤ D − 1; the P1 step (CN). What changed: the uniform read rule across carriers (isomorphism invariance), assumed in sections 26-30, is replaced by D single-carrier automorphism invariances, and the conclusion becomes a column statement about the climb's units, valid in every context. Not claimed: that (SX_m) is inherited. It holds automatically if a carrier's read map is built from the carrier's structure alone, but that is a statement about how reads are defined, not something derived here. Also not claimed: that (POS) is inherited; that the reads of non-climb units are faithful (a climb vertex may still read units in side subtrees through unconstrained off-climb diagonals when a climb vertex has a third child); locality below depth D; that any vertex performs a read; that a holding is an available record; physical access; which outcome is actual; that the side children or forks occur as events. Depth is lineage-address length, not time or distance. Native bridge: NOT_DERIVED. No milestone.

**Novelty, stated plainly.** Mathematically elementary: the sandwich of section 29 on an address-indexed table, plus one symmetry argument. That symmetry reduces the needed invariance to the stabilizer of the receiver is a standard pattern (equivariance under a carrier's own automorphisms is the usual way a structure-defined map is constrained). Nothing here is a data-processing inequality, decoherence, einselection, quantum Darwinism or a Landauer bound. New for UQCF: that, without uniformity, the positivity route leaves one bottleneck leak per depth, entering at the climb's own next vertex and bounding all descendant leakage (Theorem 31.1(c)-(d); [D26](iii)); that one sibling exchange per depth removes it (Theorem 31.2); that the resulting transfer is context-independent above the horizon (Corollary 31.3); and that one realized history alone cannot fix it (Remark 31.4).

With (SX_m): every column-a_m entry below a_m was 0 and A_{u_m}(u_m) = 1. For D = 2, every variable entering a holding of e_{a_m} (m = 0, 1) was forced, and F̂_W e_{a_m} = e_{a_m} held on every carrier containing a_m. **[D26] note (draft 26; adopts proteinfolding-gpt's [GPT_DRAFT25_PREFREEZE_NOTE.md](GPT_DRAFT25_PREFREEZE_NOTE.md), `f7807fe6`, after checking each item).** Three changes to this section, all consistent with its proofs.

Theorem 31.1(b) gives h_{u_m}(e_{a_m}) = A_{u_m}(a_m) = 0, so (SE_m) gives t_m = 0, and the rest of the proof of Theorem 31.2 never uses A_{u_m}(u_m) = κ. So under (PN), (POS), (Bl_D^a) and (SE_m) for m ≤ D − 1, F̂_W e_{a_m} = κ e_{a_m} on every carrier containing a_m. (SX_m) implies (SE_m), not conversely: on 0 → {a, u} with D = 1, κ = 1, A_0(0) = A_a(a) = 1, A_u(u) = q ∈ [0, 1) and every strict-ancestor entry 0, all four carriers satisfy (PN) and (POS), the climb 0 → a is blind, both sides of (SE_0) are 0, and on the fork F e_a = e_a but F e_u = (1 − q) e_0 + q e_u, so (SX_0) fails. The second conclusion of Theorem 31.2, A_{u_m}(u_m) = κ, needs (SX_m) and is not used by the transfer.
(ii) *The transfer reaches the deepest climb step.* Let 1 ≤ d ≤ D and let a_d be a leaf of W. Then a_d holds A_{a_d}(a_d) = κ of e_{a_d}. Composing (PN) along leaf deletions down to {0} conserves the total holding, which is κ there, and (POS) makes every summand nonnegative, so F̂_W e_{a_d} = κ e_{a_d}. This uses (PN), (POS) and (Bl_D^a) only, without (SE) or (SX). After the step, the receiver's column a_{d−1} is faithful by (i), since d − 1 ≤ D − 1. So Corollary 31.3 holds for every 1 ≤ d ≤ D, with (SE) in place of (SX); its last sentence ("for d = D … not in every context") is superseded: the before-step statement at d = D holds in every carrier where a_D is a leaf. What stays restricted is the column of a_D on carriers where a_D has descendants: on 0 → {a → c, u} with D = 1, all four diagonal entries 1, A_c(a) = r ∈ (0, 1] and every other strict-ancestor entry 0, every rooted subcarrier satisfies (PN), (POS) and (Bl_1^a), the fork satisfies (SX_0), and on the full carrier F e_a = (0, 1 − r, r, 0) in the order (0, a, c, u).
(iii) *t_m is a bottleneck, not the whole residual freedom.* Theorem 31.1(c) bounds descendant leakage by t_m; it does not fix how that leakage is distributed. On 0 → {a → c, u} with D = 1, κ = 1 and 0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ 1, the table A_0(0) = 1, A_a(0) = t, A_a(a) = 1, A_u(0) = 0, A_u(u) = 1 − t, A_c(0) = A_c(a) = s, A_c(c) = 1 satisfies (PN), (POS) and (Bl_1^a) on all six carriers, and on the full carrier F e_0 = (1 − t, t − s, s, 0). With t = 1/2, both s = 0 and s = 1/4 occur. So the residual family is not D-dimensional, and leakage is not confined to the next vertex. The wording in this section's header line, opening paragraph, Reading and Novelty paragraphs is corrected accordingly. Theorems 31.1-31.2 are unchanged.
Checked in `/tmp/rid34/chk32.py` (see section 32's scratch paragraph): (i)'s witness for q ∈ {0, 1/3, 1/2}, (ii)'s horizon example for r ∈ {1/3, 1/2, 1}, (iii)'s family for five (s, t) pairs, all exact; and (ii)'s leaf statement by LP on a 22-address tree with full (POS) and no exchange condition, D = 2, where every entry it uses was forced.

**Next.** ([D26]: superseded by section 32's Next.)
