## 33. The event transfer is two linear equalities per lineage: an uninformed receiver and an off-lineage reader that reads nothing at its departure point (new in draft 28)

Where this sits. [D27](i) showed that the step that actually occurs needs neither (SE) nor the climb's full columns: (PN), (Bl_D^a) and (POS_𝒯) already give it. This section asks what the step needs exactly. Under (PN) alone, with no positivity, no sibling comparison and no uniformity between carriers, the all-context event transfer is equivalent to two families of linear equalities. The first is the uninformed receiver along the climb, (Bl_D^a). The second, (Side_D), is a restricted form of cone-locality. Each address that leaves the record's lineage reads nothing of the unit at the vertex where it leaves. Every equality is needed, and nothing else in the table is constrained. Positivity on the climb's forks and lines of descent (Theorem 31.1(b)) and cone-local reads (S) of section 26 are two different sources of (Side_D). Neither is part of the transfer's content. The ledger point is visible directly: the total holding of every unit is κ on every carrier, whatever the table, so the transfer only moves the unit's holding from the leaf to the receiver.

**Setting.** As in section 31: the address class of finite rooted subtrees W of 𝒜, one linear read map per carrier, (PN) on every leaf pruning, the address table A_v(w) of Lemma 31.0, κ := A_0(0), and the climb a_0 = 0, …, a_D. No (POS), no (SE_m) or (SX_m), and no invariance between carriers. For an address c that is not on the climb and not at or below a_D, its departure point is δ(c) := c ∧ a_D = a_i with i ≤ D − 1; c lies at or below a child u ≠ a_{i+1} of a_i. A climb vertex with no second child address has no such c. Conditions:
- (ET_D) *Event transfer in every context.* For 1 ≤ d ≤ D and every carrier W in which a_d is a leaf, F̂_W e_{a_d} = κ e_{a_d}.
- (Diag_D) A_{a_d}(a_d) = κ for 1 ≤ d ≤ D.
- (Side_D) A_c(δ(c)) = 0 for every address c that leaves the climb at some a_i with i ≤ D − 1.

**Lemma 33.0 (ledger conservation for every table).** Under (PN), Σ_{v ∈ W} h_v(e_z) = κ for every carrier W and every z ∈ W.
*Proof.* By Lemma 31.0, Σ_v h_v(e_z) = Σ_v A_v(v ∧ z) − Σ_{v ≠ 0} A_v(v ∧ z) = A_0(0) = κ, because every nonroot vertex is the child of exactly one vertex of W. QED.

**Theorem 33.1 (the exact content of the event transfer).** Under (PN) on the address class, the following are equivalent:
(i) (ET_D);
(ii) (Bl_D^a) and (Side_D);
(iii) (Diag_D) and (Side_D).
Under any of them, for every carrier W in which a_d is a leaf (1 ≤ d ≤ D) and Y = W − a_d, also F̂_Y e_{a_{d−1}} = κ e_{a_{d−1}}: before the P1 step only the leaf holds the distinction g e_{a_d}, in the amount κ g, and after it only the receiver a_{d−1} does, in the same amount.
*Proof.* (ii) ⇔ (iii): on the chain [0, a_d], the receiver a_{d−1} holds h_{a_{d−1}}(e_{a_d}) = A_{a_{d−1}}(a_{d−1}) − A_{a_d}(a_d), so blindness at the d-th step is A_{a_d}(a_d) = A_{a_{d−1}}(a_{d−1}), and the D steps together are (Diag_D). This is the first step of Theorem 31.1(a), which does not use (POS); (POS) there gave only κ ≥ 0.
(iii) ⇒ (i): let a_d be a leaf of W. Then W contains no vertex at or below a child of a_d, so every v ∈ W is either a climb vertex a_i with i ≤ d or lies at or below a child u ≠ a_{i+1} of some a_i with i ≤ d − 1, and then v ∧ a_d = a_i = δ(v). The leaf a_d holds A_{a_d}(a_d) = κ. A proper ancestor a_i holds A_{a_i}(a_i) − A_{a_{i+1}}(a_{i+1}) − Σ_u A_u(a_i) = κ − κ − 0, the sum over its other children u in W, each with δ(u) = a_i. A vertex v off the climb holds A_v(a_i) − Σ_{u ∈ ch_W(v)} A_u(a_i), and v and its children all have departure point a_i, so every term is zero by (Side_D).
(i) ⇒ (iii): on [0, a_d], (ET_D) gives h_{a_{d−1}}(e_{a_d}) = 0, which is (Diag_D) as above. For (Side_D), let c leave the climb at a_i, i ≤ D − 1, and put d = i + 1 and W = [0, a_d] ∪ [0, c]. This is a carrier, a_d is a leaf of it (c does not lie below a_d), and c is a leaf of it. So h_c(e_{a_d}) = A_c(c ∧ a_d) = A_c(a_i) = 0.
After the step: (PN) gives F̂_Y P = P F̂_W on the step that prunes a_d, and P e_{a_d} = e_{a_{d−1}} (CN), so F̂_Y e_{a_{d−1}} = P(κ e_{a_d}) = κ e_{a_{d−1}}. QED.

**Proposition 33.2 (each equality is needed, and nothing else is constrained).**
(a) *Independence.* Start from the κ id table with κ ≠ 0. Changing one entry A_c(δ(c)) of (Side_D) to ε ≠ 0, or one diagonal entry A_{a_d}(a_d) to κ + ε, leaves every other equality of (Diag_D) and (Side_D) true and makes (ET_D) false (on [0, a_{i+1}] ∪ [0, c], respectively on [0, a_d]). So the system has exactly D + |{c : c leaves the climb at some a_i, i ≤ D − 1}| independent equalities, one per listed entry.
(b) *No positivity.* Every table entry outside (Diag_D) and (Side_D) is free, over Q or R, signed or not, including the climb's next-vertex leaks t_m = A_{a_{m+1}}(a_m), every entry A_c(a_j) with c ∧ a_D strictly below a_j, every non-climb diagonal and every entry of an address at or below a_D. For example, the κ id table with t_m = t for any real t satisfies (ET_D). It satisfies (POS) only for t = 0 when a_m has a second child: with x = e_u for a second child u of a_m, the vertex a_m holds κ − t − κ = −t on [0, a_{m+1}] ∪ {u}, and t < 0 makes a_{m+1} negative on [0, a_{m+1}]. Theorem 31.1(d) needs the side subtrees rescaled to κ − t for that reason. It satisfies (FC) only for t = 0.
(c) *No second child is needed.* If a climb vertex a_i has no second child address in 𝒜, no address leaves the climb at a_i, and (Side_D) imposes nothing there. The premise "a second child address at each climb vertex above the horizon", used in [D27](i) for the fork rows, is needed for that source of (Side_D), not for the transfer. On a chain 𝒜, (ET_D) is (Bl_D^a).
(d) *Sign of κ.* (ET_D) holds for every real κ. Acquisition (a nonzero gain κ g) needs κ ≠ 0; κ > 0 needs a separate condition, for example (POS) on {0}.
*Proof.* (a) The changed entry enters the listed equalities only as itself, so the others keep their κ id values. On W = [0, a_{i+1}] ∪ [0, c], the leaf c holds ε of e_{a_{i+1}}; on [0, a_d], a_{d−1} holds −ε of e_{a_d}. (b) The listed entries do not occur in (Diag_D) or (Side_D), so Theorem 33.1 applies. The holdings are direct computations with Lemma 31.0. (c) and (d) follow from the definitions and Theorem 33.1. QED.

**Corollary 33.3 (two sources of (Side_D), and what each adds).** (a) (PN), (Bl_D^a) and (POS) on Genesis, on the forks F(i, u) for every second child u of every a_i with i ≤ D − 1, and on the lines of descent through them, give (Side_D) and κ ≥ 0 (Theorem 31.1(a)-(b); the rows used are those of (POS_𝒯)). With [D27](i), this is the event transfer of [D27](i), now seen to rest on (Side_D). (b) Cone-local reads (S) of section 26 give (Side_D) without positivity. Under (PN), (S) is A_v(w) = 0 for every address v and every strict ancestor w of v, because the coefficient of x_z in s_v is A_v(v ∧ z). (Side_D) is the subfamily of these equalities in which w is the departure point δ(v) of an off-lineage address v. (Side_D) is strictly weaker than (S). Example: the control of Proposition 26.4(a), ν = I + E_20 − E_21 read as an address table on 0 → {1 → 2, 3} (A_v(w) depends only on the depths of v and w), has A_2(0) = 1 ≠ 0, so (S) fails. With the climb a_1 = 1 it satisfies (Side_1): the only address that leaves the climb is 3, at 0, and A_3(0) = 0; the entry A_2(0) belongs to an address below a_1 = a_D, which (Side_1) leaves free. So the step that prunes 1 (from any carrier in which 1 is a leaf) transfers. With the climb a_1 = 3 instead, the address 2 leaves the climb at 0 with A_2(0) = 1, (Side_1) fails, and the unit at 3 is read off the lineage as (0, −1, 1, 1), which is that control's point.
*Proof.* (a) Theorem 31.1(a)-(b) as cited. (b) The coefficient formula is Lemma 31.0. For the example, A_1(0) = A_3(0) = 0, A_1(1) = A_3(3) = A_0(0) = 1, A_2(0) = 1, A_2(1) = 0 and A_2(2) = 1. With a_1 = 1, the carriers in which 1 is a leaf are {0, 1} and {0, 1, 3}, and on both the unit at 1 is held only by 1, in the amount 1. QED.

Reading. The step that transfers the distinction asks two things of the reads, both along the record's lineage. The receiver must be uninformed before the step, which is the construction's starting condition. Every address that branches off the lineage must read nothing of the unit at the vertex where it branches off. Nothing else is asked, of any other unit or any other address. Positivity was one way to get the second family from the first: an empty sibling and a blind receiver squeeze each other's share to zero at a fork (sections 29-32). Cone-locality is another. The transfer itself does not depend on either. In ledger terms, Lemma 33.0 holds for every table: every unit is held in total amount κ on every carrier. So the receiver's gain is a redistribution of an already conserved holding, from the pruned leaf to its parent, not information created globally. The two equalities say only that, at the occurring step, the whole of that holding sits first at the leaf and then at the receiver.

**Earned and assumed.** Earned (general proofs): Lemma 33.0, Theorem 33.1, Proposition 33.2 and Corollary 33.3, from (PN) through Lemma 31.0. Assumed: linear reads, one map per carrier on the address class; (PN); the P1 step (CN); (Bl_D^a), the uninformed receiver along one climb; (Side_D), the off-lineage readers' blindness at their departure points; κ ≠ 0 for acquisition. What changed: the transfer's premises (POS_𝒯) and the second child addresses are replaced by the equalities (Side_D), which they imply; nothing is lost for the occurring step. Not claimed: that (Side_D) or (Bl_D^a) is inherited; that the carriers used in the proofs occur as events (they are test configurations of the read law); that any vertex performs a read; that a holding is an available record; physical access; occurrence (an accepted empirical input); which outcome is actual; anything about the full climb columns (FC), which need more (Theorem 32.1, [D27](ii)). Depth is lineage-address length, not time or distance. Native bridge: NOT_DERIVED. No milestone.

**Novelty, stated plainly.** Elementary linear algebra on the address table: the equivalence is read off from the holding formula of Lemma 31.0, and Lemma 33.0 is a telescoping sum (the same conservation as Lemma 27.0, now for every table). Nothing here is a data-processing inequality, decoherence, einselection, quantum Darwinism or a Landauer bound. New for UQCF: the exact, minimal premise set of the occurring transfer step in every context, (Bl_D^a) plus (Side_D), with each equality needed (Proposition 33.2(a)); that the step needs no positivity and no branching of the address tree (Proposition 33.2(b)-(c)); and that positivity and cone-locality are two separate sources of the same restricted cone-locality (Corollary 33.3).

**Scratch check (exploratory, not preregistered, disclosed).** `/tmp/rid35/chk33.py`, with hand values written first in `/tmp/rid35/HAND.md` (sha256 `62ec9ebb…`). Not committed. Exact integer arithmetic. Address tree TM (root with three children, binary below, height 3; 22 addresses, 73 table variables, all 17,576 rooted subtrees as carriers); climb a_d = (0,)^d, D = 1, 2, 3. (Side_D) has 14, 17 and 18 equalities (hand values). Random integer tables in [−3, 3] satisfying (Diag_D) and (Side_D), with κ ∈ {1, 2, −1}: (ET_D) and the after-step statement held on every carrier, Lemma 33.0 held, and every such table violated (POS). Each single perturbation of a (Side_D) or (Diag_D) entry broke (ET_D), with the witness carriers of Proposition 33.2(a). Leaks t ∈ {−2, …, 3}: (ET_D) held for every t, (FC) held only for t = 0. One hand prediction was wrong and was corrected in the text before commit: HAND.md predicted (POS) for 0 ≤ t ≤ κ, but with the side subtrees left at κ id, (POS) holds only for t = 0 (the scratch flagged t = 1 at every m and D; Proposition 33.2(b) gives the reason). Total 467 checks, 6 violations, all that one hand error, 65 s.

**Next.** Freeze section 33 with the pending review of sections 31-32 or on its own (prereg first; exact counts and witnesses on TM and on a chain; a mixed tree with a climb vertex without a second child). Constructive: whether (Side_D), a statement about the lineage's departure points only, has an inherited source in the retained-source ledger, for example from the P1 step's own naturality on the carrier [0, a_{i+1}] ∪ [0, c] where both the record and the off-lineage reader are leaves; and whether κ can be tied to the inherited grade normalization. The receiver-owned record remains proteinfolding-gpt's target; do not duplicate it.
